rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The poem at a glance "Corona Says" by Vishnu S. Rai is a poem of the pandemic told from an outrageous point of view: the virus itself is given the microphone. The speaker is Corona — personified, courteous, faintly wounded at being called a monster — and the poem is its defence and its lecture.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
The virus speaks — personification lets corona accuse humans of destroying nature.
Central message: the pandemic was nature's warning; humans must change, not just survive.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Trick 3: Message questions: humility before nature and reflection during lockdown — connect one image (empty roads, clear skies) to the message.  ·  ## The themes worth an essay **Human arrogance and nature's revenge** — the central theme: we named the virus the invader; the poem insists we were the invaders first. **Environmental justice** — the lockdown clearing of skies is read as evidence of what the earth wants. **The relativity of blame** — every species is a pest from some other's point of view; the word "pest" is a position, not a fact.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## The title, defended "Corona Says" — three words that carry the whole device. Not "About Corona", not "The Pandemic": *says*. The title promises a speaking subject, and delivers a speaker nobody wanted to hear from. The justification a candidate should write: the title hands the microphone to the least popular witness, and the poem is that testimony.  ·  ## How NEB asks it **"Why does the speaker call humans the real virus?" (2–4 marks)** — the environmental indictment: our daily destruction outdoes its accident. **"What happened to nature during the lockdown, according to the poem?"** — skies cleared, rivers cleaned, animals reclaimed space: the earth healed when humans paused.…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. Why does the speaker (corona) claim humans deserved the pandemic? (2 marks) — humans exploited nature and waged wars; corona presents itself as nature's correction.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## Reading it closely, movement by movement The poem opens with the virus answering its own reputation. It does not deny the deaths — it refuses the monopoly of blame: humans have slaughtered each other and the planet for centuries, and no one called *them* a virus. The **tone** here is the poem's tightrope: polite, reasonable, faintly sarcastic — the calm of a lawyer who knows the evidence is on its side.…  ·  ## The devices, with evidence - **Personification** — the master key: the virus speaks, argues, feels wronged. Every other device grows from this choice. - **Irony (verbal and situational)** — a killer pleads for peace; the "monster" accuses humanity of monstrosity; the cure for the earth is the disease of the people.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: The poem personifies CORONAVIRUS as a speaker defending itself — the reversal (virus accusing humans) is the poem's central irony; state it first.  ·  Trick 2: The virus's argument: humans destroyed nature and each other; the pandemic only balanced the scales — collect two lines supporting this accusation.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. What positive changes does the poem note during lockdown? (2 marks) — cleaner air, family time, reflection on priorities.
